title: M7 — Power cord grommet

# M7: Mount the rubber grommet for the power cord

> *Mount the rubber grommet in the ½" hole in the center of the rear flange of the chassis.* — manual page 5

## What you're doing physically

A small **rubber grommet** (donut-shaped) goes into the ½" hole on the rear flange of the chassis. The grommet snaps in — push it through the hole until both sides of its lip catch on either side of the chassis metal. No tools or fasteners needed.

The power cord will eventually pass through the center of this grommet in step 65 of the wiring procedure.

## Why a grommet

The chassis hole has sharp metal edges. Without a grommet, the power cord's insulation would be slowly cut through by chassis vibration over years of use. Eventually the bare conductor could touch the chassis, creating a shock hazard.

The rubber grommet:

1. **Protects the cord insulation** from the sharp chassis edge.
2. **Adds strain relief** — the grommet grips the cord enough that pulling on the cord doesn't immediately yank the internal connections off the fuse / switch.
3. **Provides electrical insulation** at the chassis penetration point — extra layer of safety if the cord's outer jacket ever cracks.

The kit's grommet is small (½") because the power cord is fairly thin. Modern 3-prong cords are sometimes slightly fatter and need a slightly larger grommet — see [3-prong cord modification](../../modifications/3-prong-cord.md) if you're upgrading to a grounded cord.

## When to install

The grommet goes in NOW (during mechanical assembly) so the chassis hole is sealed by the time the power cord goes through it later. If you skip this and try to add the grommet AFTER the cord is in place, you'll be wrestling with a stiff rubber donut around a stiff plastic-jacketed cable in cramped quarters — annoying and error-prone.
